title: ChatGPT for Mac Adds Computer History Feature, Replacing Screenshot-Based Chronicle
excerpt: OpenAI's new opt-in feature tracks app and website activity through interaction events instead of screenshots, turning daily workflows into searchable AI memories.
body:
• OpenAI has launched Computer History, a new ChatGPT feature for macOS that turns app and website activity into searchable memories — without taking screenshots.
  • The feature replaces the earlier Chronicle research preview, using interaction events like clicks, typing, and app switches instead of screen captures.
  • Computer History is off by default and available only to ChatGPT Pro, Business, and Enterprise users on macOS, with no access in the EU, UK, or Switzerland.

OpenAI has rolled out Computer History, a new opt-in feature for its ChatGPT desktop app on macOS that tracks user activity across apps and websites and converts it into memories that ChatGPT and Codex can reference in future conversations.

The feature replaces Chronicle, an earlier research preview that relied on periodic screenshots to build context. Computer History takes a fundamentally different approach: it records interaction events — clicks, typing, keyboard shortcuts, and app switches — rather than capturing the screen or audio. It does not require Screen Recording permission, a change that addresses one of the primary privacy concerns with its predecessor.

How Computer History Works

Once enabled, Computer History creates a stream of interaction events from allowed apps and websites. The system periodically processes these events into text summaries and local memory files stored as plain-text Markdown on the user's Mac. Temporary event files are retained for up to 48 hours, while generated memories persist until the user deletes them.

https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2087996496088297746

OpenAI processes the event files on its servers to generate the memories, then deletes the raw event data. The company says it does not retain event files after processing unless required by law and does not use them for model training.

Users can ask natural-language questions about their recent work — "What was I working on before my last break?" or "Give me a list of tasks I've worked on today and their status." When a file, Slack conversation, or Google Doc is more relevant, ChatGPT can use the history to identify the source and read it directly.

"Computer History replaces the earlier Chronicle research preview, but it is a rebuilt system rather than a rename. Chronicle used screenshots. Computer History records interaction events and does not capture your screen or audio."

— OpenAI Developer Documentation

Privacy Controls and Availability

Computer History is off by default. ChatGPT Pro users can enable it in Settings under Integrations, while Business and Enterprise users require administrator approval before opting in. The feature is not available in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom.

Users control which apps and websites contribute to their history, with options to exclude specific apps or allow only selected ones. Private-mode web browsing is never included. Collection can be paused, resumed, or stopped entirely from the macOS menu bar, and users can clear their history for the last 10 minutes, last hour, last day, or all time.

Event data is stored within the ChatGPT App Group on macOS, which prevents other apps from accessing it without explicit permission. OpenAI acknowledges that Computer History increases the risk of prompt injection — malicious instructions in a visited website could potentially influence ChatGPT's behavior.

From Screenshots to Keystroke Logging

The shift from Chronicle's screenshot-based approach to Computer History's interaction-event model represents a trade-off. Chronicle drew criticism for its screen-capture methodology, which echoed the controversy around Microsoft's Recall feature. Screenshots captured everything visible on screen, including sensitive information from emails, banking apps, and private messages.

Computer History's event-based approach avoids screen captures entirely but effectively logs user interactions at a granular level — tracking what users click, type, and navigate across their Mac. The Register described this shift as moving from "Recall-style screenshot surveillance" to "friendly keylogging," noting that the distinction in privacy impact may be less clear-cut than it appears.

The feature also introduces workflow automation capabilities. When Computer History detects repeatable patterns in a user's work, it can suggest creating a skill or automation through Codex, turning observed workflows into reusable processes.

Looking Ahead

Computer History is currently limited to macOS, with no announced timeline for Windows support. The feature requires ChatGPT Pro ($200/month), Business, or Enterprise subscriptions, putting it out of reach for free and Plus users. OpenAI has not indicated whether a more accessible version is planned.

The launch continues OpenAI's push to make ChatGPT deeply integrated with users' daily computing workflows, following earlier features like Work with Apps on macOS and improved chat history search. For users comfortable with the privacy trade-offs, Computer History could eliminate the need to re-explain context across conversations — but the line between helpful memory and surveillance remains a point of debate.
nri_angle: Relevant to Indian-origin tech professionals and developers who use ChatGPT on Mac for work, particularly those working in privacy-conscious enterprise environments.
